segments.text: Your job is demanding more than your time, it's stealing your peace.
You fear that drawing a line will get you fired, but staying silent guarantees burnout.
The anxiety of overcommitting is real, yet the cost of saying yes to everything is your own well-being.
Marcus Aurelius faced constant political games and manipulation, yet he maintained his composure by focusing only on what he could control.
This is the dichotomy of control: your effort and character are yours to manage, while others reactions and office politics are not.
By detaching your self-worth from external approval, you become harder to provoke or manipulate.
Translate this into a concrete routine: when a deadline is shifted or a request feels unreasonable, take a deliberate pause before responding.
Do not react with ego or immediate agreement; instead, state your current capacity clearly and professionally.
Treat stressful meetings as training reps for patience, using the moment to practice calm judgment rather than emotional defense.
Subscribe for more ways to protect your mind without losing your career.
